query: group antenatal care attendance cost-effectiveness community hubs deprived areas young women migrants
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of maternity care research
gradeRationale: A few trials and reviews suggest better attendance, so certainty is low.
synthesis: The search did not run, so four leads are recalled from memory: a randomised trial in urban clinics, a review of attendance and outcomes, an undated economic evaluation and an interview study with migrant women. None has been retrieved or checked.

items.title: Group prenatal care and attendance: a randomised trial in urban clinics
items.keyFindings: Group care increased adequate attendance compared with individual care.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; not retrieved.

items.title: Group antenatal care: a systematic review of attendance, outcomes and experience
items.keyFindings: Attendance improved in most studies; clinical outcomes were inconsistent.

items.title: Economic evaluation of group antenatal care in a publicly funded service
items.keyFindings: Reported a cost per additional woman with adequate attendance, with wide uncertainty.
items.limitations: No year given; model inputs not described.

items.title: Experiences of migrant women in group antenatal care: an interview study
items.keyFindings: Women valued peer support but needed interpreters in every session.

summary: Four unchecked leads after a failed search.
